scope: Consumer executor, integration diff and compatibility with the current producer interface. Producer correctness, live certification and proof acceptance remain separate.

reviewed_boundaries.result: The caller must supply the independently retained hash of the capture-specific binding. An existing RUN must bind its same complete file identity. The fixed manifest path, every manifest member and the exact flat protocol namespace are authenticated, as are the certificate, history and current guard. Only then does verify_recovery invoke the fixed verify entrypoint in an isolated, no-site, no-bytecode interpreter, supplying the pinned certificate hash and byte count. After the call it authenticates these artifacts again, checks scope flags, guard differences and the response bindings.

The preserved original pilot and continuation contexts remain identical, including the old guard. The recovery response must agree with them and the authenticated package. The new RUN and prefix explicitly keep both guard identities, the certificate, history and the failed-old-validator flag. The consumer invokes original lower-level raw-step validators only after caller-bound recovery verification. It cross-checks all 24 ordered seals, both historical stop indexes, original counters, the failed normal command/log/source/object state and all 113 raw pins. Its 125 source/object rows, declared imports and actual paths must agree with the history view and original inputs. More distant historical families, the full ten-root equality and their frozen inputs depend on the independently reviewed producer.

The same bound recovery view is reverified before and after every new proof process, and before and after final export/retained verification. Input hashes, namespace isolation and original compiler/checker identities are rechecked. Launch witnesses remain exclusive and flushed before launch, and ordinary sections for revalidating three ordered mode receipts remain intact. Verify still opens the stage lock read-only, requires established evidence/directories and uses archive readback.

The archive plan includes the operator binding, all listed producer protocol source/data, its manifest, current guard, history and certificate, as well as the repaired source/object, audit, consumer, launch witnesses and per-mode evidence. It pins the original guard/snapshot and preserved raw history through the contexts; its separately retained original archive is referenced. The new SUCCESS covers exactly one owner and three checks. No old SUCCESS is manufactured and P2_6_complete remains false.

Compared the draft producer argv, schema/flags, output paths and response fields against the consumer, including full original identities, state.objects representation, failure pins and the 117+8 dependency shape. Found no consumer/producer schema mismatch. The producer is not certified by this review.
